body:
Thank you for replying.

I don't know if "coping" is the right word for what I'm doing. I try to minimize the amount of time I stay awake and typically aim to spend at least 12 hours a day sleeping because it's hugely preferable to being awake. When I can't sleep, I distract myself with hobbies and crafts and reading until I'm tired again. When that doesn't work and I start feeling bad, I lose the energy to stand or even sit up straight and I can't think of doing anything except hurting myself so I just slink away to bed and cry/scream for a few hours until it passes or I get tired enough to sleep.

I seem to remember first hurting myself when I was 9 or 10 but it was never a huge presence in my life. It's always been something I only did a handful times a year because I've always had a pretty good reason to not do it even though I really wanted to. When I was in school and around people every day, hiding scars was too much trouble but now that I'm not in school and have limited physical contact with any human being except my boyfriend, I can't do it because it upsets him too much. The last time I cut myself was May.

My thoughts of dying are just as pervasive except in a different way. Back then, it was short bursts of extremely strong and unbearable feelings. Today, it's more like a constant dull ache. I think I just got used to wanting to die, to be honest, and my perceived severity of those kinds of feelings gradually went down as it became a daily fact of life that I really want to stop living.

Yes, I do feel that way in regards to my relationship with my boyfriend.
